title: Euro-area household expectations remain stable in aggregate while income and credit exposure diverge sharply by position
source_unit: European Central Bank, Consumer Expectations Survey results – August 2026
geography: Euro area; adults in Belgium, Germany, Ireland, Greece, Spain, France, Italy, the Netherlands, Austria, Portugal and Finland

denominator.unit: approximately adult consumers in the ECB monthly online survey across 11 euro-area countries

past_inflation_perception.unit: median percent perceived inflation over the previous 12 months

one_year_inflation_expectation.unit: median percent expected inflation over the next 12 months

three_year_inflation_expectation.unit: median percent expected inflation three years ahead

five_year_inflation_expectation.unit: median percent expected inflation five years ahead

income_quintile_exposure.value: respondents in the bottom income quintile continued to report higher inflation perceptions and expectations than those in the top quintile

observations.method: ECB monthly online Consumer Expectations Survey; aggregate results are reported as medians unless otherwise indicated and are drawn from around 19,000 adults across 11 euro-area countries.
observations.uncertainty: The release reports perceived and expected inflation, not individually verified price baskets, realized inflation exposure, or causal effects of income position on expectations.
observations.subgroup: Adults in the bottom and top income quintiles as defined by the survey.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher expectations among lower-income respondents may reflect different consumption baskets, local prices, financial vulnerability, or information exposure rather than only objective inflation differences.

denominator.unit: approximately adult consumers in the ECB monthly online survey across 11 euro-area countries

expected_nominal_income_growth.unit: median expected nominal income growth over the next 12 months

bottom_quintile_income_expectation.unit: average expected nominal income growth in the bottom income quintile

top_quintile_income_expectation.unit: average expected nominal income growth in the top income quintile

expected_nominal_spending_growth.unit: median expected nominal spending growth over the next 12 months

expectations_gap.value: expected spending growth remains above expected nominal income growth, while the aggregate expectation is unchanged

observations.method: ECB monthly online Consumer Expectations Survey with income-quintile comparisons.
observations.uncertainty: Expected income and spending are self-reported nominal expectations; the release does not identify whether households will use savings, credit, reduced quantities, or substitution to bridge the gap.
observations.subgroup: Euro-area consumers overall and the bottom versus top income quintiles.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher expected income growth in the bottom quintile can reflect catch-up expectations or composition differences and does not establish improved real purchasing power.

denominator.unit: approximately adult consumers in the ECB monthly online survey across 11 euro-area countries

expected_unemployment_rate.unit: median expected unemployment rate in 12 months

bottom_quintile_expected_unemployment.unit: average expected unemployment rate in 12 months among the bottom income quintile

top_quintile_expected_unemployment.unit: average expected unemployment rate in 12 months among the top income quintile

expected_home_price_growth.unit: median expected home-price growth over the next 12 months

bottom_quintile_home_price_expectation.unit: average expected home-price growth in the lowest income quintile

top_quintile_home_price_expectation.unit: average expected home-price growth in the highest income quintile

observations.method: ECB monthly online Consumer Expectations Survey; housing and labour indicators are reported as survey expectations, not administrative forecasts.
observations.uncertainty: The survey does not observe actual unemployment, home transactions, affordability, housing tenure, or individual exposure to job loss or price change.
observations.subgroup: Euro-area consumers overall and income-quintile groups.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower-income respondents may expect faster home-price growth because they face greater affordability pressure or because of different local-market composition; the result is not evidence of a uniform housing market.

observations.period: August 2026; mortgage rates and credit access

denominator.unit: approximately adult consumers in the ECB monthly online survey across 11 euro-area countries

expected_mortgage_rate.unit: median expected mortgage interest rate in 12 months

bottom_quintile_expected_mortgage_rate.unit: average expected mortgage interest rate in 12 months among the bottom income quintile

top_quintile_expected_mortgage_rate.unit: average expected mortgage interest rate in 12 months among the top income quintile

credit_tightening.value: the net percentage reporting tighter past credit access and expecting tighter future credit access both declined from July

credit_asymmetry.value: credit conditions eased in aggregate while expected mortgage costs remained 1.3 percentage points higher for the bottom than the top income quintile

observations.method: ECB monthly online Consumer Expectations Survey; credit-access measures are net balances and mortgage figures are expected rates.
observations.uncertainty: The release does not identify who is applying for credit, actual approval or denial, mortgage type, lender pricing, debt service, or whether expectations change behaviour.
observations.subgroup: Euro-area consumers, with mortgage-rate comparisons by income quintile.
observations.counterinterpretation: Income-group differences may partly reflect tenure and borrower composition; expected mortgage rates cannot be interpreted as realized borrowing costs for all households.

related_sources.claim: Official ECB August 2026 Consumer Expectations Survey release, including sample frame, income quintiles, inflation, income, spending, labour, housing and credit expectations.
ECB Data Portal provides the associated aggregate country and euro-area time series.

boundary: This record adds a distributional expectations route: lower-income euro-area consumers report higher inflation, unemployment and mortgage-rate expectations while aggregate income, spending and credit-access expectations remain comparatively stable. The monthly online survey is broad and repeated but self-reported; it does not measure realized prices, borrowing, spending, employment, housing transactions, or causal household outcomes.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: ECB primary release reviewed for survey frame, fieldwork timing, income-quintile comparisons, inflation, income, spending, unemployment, housing, mortgage and credit-access measures.
